move.subject: Re: Quote from Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH: Ravensteiner cuts the seal allocation
move.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.
Thank you for your open message about the capacity situation on the mechanical seal. We understand that your lines are fully booked and that you must prioritise customers who commit firmly. We are ready to be such a customer: we offer a binding annual volume covering our full need over a two-year term, at your standard lead time. In return we ask for a guaranteed allocation at today's price, continuing the moderation that has served us both well.

Our data shows a different picture on some points:
Our demand forecast for this part has risen 10.1% (fc:340010@2026-09).
Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 29.89 per unit (po:4500014436-10, po:4500014383-10, po:4500014337-10).
Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 79.5% (sc:70410@2026Q3).

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation.

We note your proposed volume of 23,400 units and the 24-month contract term. Due to our current capacity utilization, historical price levels are not feasible. Our price reflects our costs; our calculation stays internal.

We offer EUR 31.90 per unit based on your requested terms, specifically a price of €31.90 per unit, Lieferzeit 56 days, a volume of 23400 pcs per year, a contract term of 24 months. Our Lieferzeit is 56 days. This offer remains valid for 30 days.

Which volume can you commit to?

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Monika Zellner
Segment Manager, Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

decisions.why: final_offer; C 1,532,386 below the limit inf

key_points: Bottleneck single source with supplier-owned tooling and no alternative. Securing full coverage of the need comes first.

The supplier wants binding long-term commitments rather than cash. Offer the full need of the volume options as binding, plus a contract of twenty-four months, in exchange for the current price and a guaranteed allocation.
Accept its own lead time of forty-two days, which equals our need lead time. Do not ask for a shorter one.
It historically settles well below its ask, often at zero. Keep moves within its approval band to avoid committee delays.
Should-cost is used only if it argues cost. Against a capacity-full supplier it would be dismissed as theoretical.
The price is fixed per calendar year, and the effective date is fixed at the next year start.
plan.stance_why: This is a secure_supply case: single source, supplier-owned tooling, no fallback supplier, and a fallback price far above the current price. The supplier is capacity-full and can deprioritise us, and a margin charge applies if it is left unhealthy. We open close to the current price and trade commitment rather than squeezing.

levers.why: Our forecast has risen, a checkable fact. Paired with a binding volume, it gives the supplier the planning security it asks for.

argument.sentence: Our demand forecast for this part has risen 10.1% (fc:340010@2026-09).
argument.note: Snapshot 2026-09: 21310 for the next 12 months against 19360 ordered in the last 12 months (requested dates); shared with suppliers: True. More volume is worth more to it.

levers.why: Verifiable proof that the current price is the stable reference for this part.

argument.sentence: Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 29.89 per unit (po:4500014436-10, po:4500014383-10, po:4500014337-10).
argument.note: What we pay now: [29.89, 29.89, 29.89] per unit (2026-08-27 to 2026-09-21); anchors any increase.

levers.why: Context showing that moderation is the shared basis of the relationship. Use it as framing, not as a jab.

argument.note: 3 renewals: asked +3.8% on average, settled +1.1% (gap 2.7 pp); last 2025-11-23: asked +2.5%, settled +0.0%. It usually settles well below its ask.

levers.why: Shows we are a reliable payer, which supports the relationship need.

argument.note: 218 invoices; we pay 2.1 days after due on average (last 12 months), 76.4% late, 0.0% over 10 days late, max 6; discounts taken 0 (0 after the period); short-paid 0. We pay reliably: a fair customer.

levers.why: A late fresh fact: delivery is below target, so an increase is not justified. Use it gently.

argument.sentence: Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 79.5% (sc:70410@2026Q3).
argument.note: Rolling 12 months to 2026-09-30: 79.5% on time against the requested date (85.9% against its own confirmed date); target 95%; peers' median 84.6%; class A green. A year earlier 78.7%.

levers.why: Any change is tied to the calendar-year price fixing.

argument.sentence: Our framework agreement fixes prices for each calendar year.
argument.note: ctr:4600070410#3.1 (price): Prices as per the price annex, fixed for each calendar year. Changes require written notice of at least 90 days before the end of the calendar year.

levers.why: Use only if it insists that costs justify an increase; it shows ample margin.

argument.sentence: Our bottom-up cost model puts the full cost of this part at EUR 24.31 per unit (cost:340010).
argument.note: Should-cost EUR 24.31 per unit (its own plant, error about 5%); its price EUR 29.89 per unit (price from 2026-01-01) is +23.0% against it.

trades.why: A binding commitment to the full need is its main currency. It covers our whole requirement and is above the must-have.
Twenty-four months captures the commitment value and secures supply over our horizon.
Accepting its standard lead time costs us nothing and meets our need.

sup:70410.opening_paragraph: Thank you for your open message about the capacity situation on the mechanical seal. We understand that your lines are fully booked and that you must prioritise customers who commit firmly. We are ready to be such a customer: we offer a binding annual volume covering our full need over a two-year term, at your standard lead time. In return we ask for a guaranteed allocation at today's price, continuing the moderation that has served us both well.
watch_for: Allocation offered only at a higher price. Respond with a small, shrinking step rather than conceding.
Index arguments on labour and rubber. Reply that, weighted by their share of cost, they support very little.
Committee delays when a move exceeds its approval band.
A declared final offer. Accept it if it is below the fallback.
An allocated volume below the must-have, or a lead time longer than our need.
A price start before the next calendar year.

risks: Losing allocation if we press too hard on price. Uncovered need would be bought at the much dearer fallback price.
Committing the full volume when past forecasts overshot. This is moderate because the need is fixed in this case.
Committee cycles slowing the negotiation. Silence could harden its offers into finals.
Evidence of its pricing flexibility under capacity scarcity is thin. The low historical settlements predate the allocation.
